clue.text: Power grab by the French pair

blocks.note: a coup is a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: A French couple seizing power together.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is two of something, a synonym for a pair.

clue.text: Python found in Gents

explanation.surface: A snake discovered in the men's lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Gents is British for a men's toilet; the python is not a snake but Graham Chapman of Monty Python.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Chapman was a member of the Monty Python comedy team, so he was a Python.

clue.text: Yorkshire river with a smell, ultimately, of waste product

blocks.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire
taken as written
the final letter of smell

explanation.surface: A northern English river that smells of sewage.

clue.text: Go into panic about old rugby player

blocks.note: to lose one's head is to panic
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.walkthrough: The O goes inside after the first two letters: LO(O)SE HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The loosehead is the prop forward on the left of the front row of a rugby scrum.

clue.text: Reserve fashion house for pigs

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a sty is a pen where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: A fashion label keeping some stock back for pigs, of all customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a noun is restraint in showing oneself, a synonym of this quality.

clue.text: Young woman working around international embassy

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the preceding words go round the next

blocks.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
I is the abbreviation for international
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A young woman with a job at a foreign embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working around' looks like one phrase, but around applies to the two outer pieces together, which enclose the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission is a delegation or embassy sent to a foreign country.

clue.text: Shot a story on film?

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits, a shot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film crew shooting a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like filming but is a measure of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a story acted out, and a film drama is a story told on screen.

clue.text: Foxy nurses shower in an unimaginative manner

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

blocks.note: foxy means cunning or sly
to lavish is to shower someone with things

explanation.surface: An alluring woman who nurses a gift-giver, done without flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like a noun for rain or washing; here it is the verb meaning to give generously.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something slavishly means copying without originality, an unimaginative manner.

clue.text: Rodney plays over there, but not too far away

definitions.text: over there, but not too far away

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters are played around with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Rodney performing just a short distance off.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old word meaning at some distance but still within sight.

clue.text: Cycling elf shows lively wit

indicators.note: cycling means the last letter is moved round to the front

blocks.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy

explanation.surface: An elf on a bike displaying sparkling humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for liveliness of mind and sparkle in conversation.

clue.text: A grotesque hole employs locals

indicators.note: something grotesque is distorted out of its natural shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word hole, rearranged
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: An ugly dive of a place that takes on staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's nearby pub, so locals are public houses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a local is the neighbourhood pub, and an alehouse is an old word for a pub.

clue.text: A trap traps American for a second time

indicators.note: to trap something is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a gin is a snare or trap for game
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Telling of a snare that has caught an American, and done it twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The American sits inside the trap: G(A)IN after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, which is doing something a second time.

clue.text: Honey bee loses head in fight

blocks.note: mel is the Latin (and pharmacists') word for honey
the word bee without its first letter

explanation.surface: A honey bee decapitated during a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Honey bee' reads as one insect, but honey and bee are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand brawl, a kind of fight.

clue.text: Present new analysis of a regime in loco

indicators.note: loco is slang for crazy, and crazy letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A political analyst offering a fresh take on a regime acting in someone's place, in loco parentis style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In loco' looks like the Latin phrase; 'in' belongs to the letters and loco means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimagine something is to interpret it afresh, offering a new analysis of it.

clue.text: Ignore constant gentle tremors

indicators.note: tremors shake things, and shaken letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to pay no attention to continual mild earth tremors.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, a synonym of ignore.

clue.text: Bits of information Berlusconi perhaps finally released

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
Silvio Berlusconi, Italian prime minister, without his last letter

explanation.surface: Details about the Italian politician finally being made public.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlusconi was an Italian prime minister notorious for sex scandals, which fits the cheeky answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bits is informal slang for the private parts, the sexual organs.

clue.text: One after the other, constantly

setter's reading: 'the other' is a coy euphemism for sex, so this is someone forever after it

explanation.surface: Things happening one after another without a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after the other' sounds like sequence; 'the other' is British slang for sex, and 'one' is a person chasing it constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is informal for a woman with an insatiable sexual appetite, someone constantly after sex.

clue.text: Queen fan brushing aside rumours, initially, of devoted way of life

indicators.note: brushing something aside removes it, so a letter is taken out
initially points to the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: a supporter of the monarchy, here the Queen
the opening letter of rumours

explanation.surface: A royalist ignoring gossip about a life of religious devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Monachist means monastic, relating to monks and their life of religious devotion.

clue.text: Tense and disillusioned German guards

indicators.note: the phrase guards the answer, holding it inside its letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A disenchanted German security guard feeling jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means nervous and uneasy, which is what tense means as an adjective.

clue.text: Record one's poem for part of TV series

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is one, plus 's
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Recording a poem to use in a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single instalment of a television series.

clue.text: Instant new look at designer's prelude is a bit rich

indicators.note: a prelude is what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: mo is British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
N is the standard abbreviation for new
to eye something is to look at it
the opening letter of designer

explanation.surface: A designer's new collection, previewed for a moment, is rather extravagant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit rich' sounds like the idiom for cheek, but here it just means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed people have plenty of money, so they are wealthy, a little rich at least.

clue.text: Gloomy medical officer got promoted

blocks.note: MO is the abbreviation for medical officer
someone who rose went up in rank

explanation.surface: An army doctor who is sullen despite his promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and ill-tempered, a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Piano in key that's lower

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the other word

blocks.note: Delete is a key on a computer keyboard
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano piece in a key pitched lower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'piano' suggest music, but the key is on a computer keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to reduce a stock, which is to lower it, used as a verb.

clue.text: Tap up American soldier that punches best

blocks.note: tops is slang for the best
a GI is a US soldier

clue.text: Rotter is assigned official? That is right

blocks.note: to be put somewhere is to be assigned there
a ref (referee) is a match official
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotter' looks like a cad, but literally it is something that makes things rot.
explanation.definitionFit: A putrefier causes decay, so it is literally a thing that rots, a 'rotter'.

clue.text: Go into hub over the pond? Not at first

blocks.note: the American spelling of a hub or centre

clue.text: Conservative with light grip

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

clue.text: Silver corroded stone

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

clue.text: Jacket Earl wears covered in gold

clue.text: Stubborn stain to be disguised

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

the final letter of magazine
